editorial:
Ever wondered what it was like to be the guy in the back of the world's most famous band? You get to see the rise of the Beatles through the eyes of Ringo Starr, and it is a total blast. Instead of focusing on the huge egos and the fighting, this movie feels like a warm hug. It shows you the funny side of fame and how Ringo just tried to keep everything together while the world went crazy around him. The vibe is light and heartfelt, making you root for the drummer who often felt like the odd man out in the group.

What really hits home is the acting, which makes Ringo feel like a real person rather than just a historical figure. The pacing is smooth, though some of the middle parts drag a bit when they talk about recording sessions. You should definitely watch this if you love music or just want a feel-good story about friendship. For the best experience, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the great colors. If you are a big fan, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a no-brainer.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a quiet scene after the band breaks up. You see Ringo looking back at his time with the group and realizing that while he wasn't the main songwriter, he was the glue that held them together. The final shot shows him playing drums in his own home, smiling and happy. It wraps up by showing that he found peace and joy on his own terms after the madness ended.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music history and underdog stories.
